title: A domain map with separable fraction fields is smooth on a principal open
statement: Let $R\to S$ be an injective finite type homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], where $R$ and $S$ are integral domains (nonzero rings in which a product is zero only if one factor is zero). Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ and $L=\operatorname{Frac}(S)$ be their fraction fields, the fields of fractions with nonzero denominators, with the induced embedding $K\to L$. If $L/K$ is separable in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension], then there exists $g\in S$, $g\ne0$, such that the composite $R\to S\to S_g$ is a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Here $S_g$ is the ring of fractions $s/g^n$ for $s\in S$ and integers $n\ge0$, with the usual fraction operations.

source.place: Tag 07ND, lemma-smooth-at-generic-point, implication from separable fraction fields to smoothness at the zero prime; smoothness at that prime is expanded as the existence of a nonzero principal localization that is smooth.

proof.text: Apply the proved affine helper RingHom.exists_nonzero_finitePresentation_localizationAway from the generic-local-finite-presentation module [lem-sbc-generic-flat-finite-presentation-lfp]. For different universes shrink S to the universe of R using Algebra.FiniteType.small and Shrink.algEquiv; transport the resulting principal localization back by IsLocalization.algEquivOfAlgEquiv. This gives a nonzero a in R with B = S[1/image(a)] finitely presented over R. Injectivity makes b = image(a) nonzero.

Put K = Frac(R) and L = Frac(S), with exactly the embedding of the hypothesis. The tower R -> K -> L agrees with R -> S -> L by IsLocalization.map_eq. L is essentially of finite type over R by localization and composition, hence over K by Algebra.EssFiniteType.of_comp. Apply separability [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] to the top intermediate field, which is finitely generated by IntermediateField.fg_top. Its separable transcendence basis yields formal smoothness over K by Mathlib Algebra.FormallySmooth.of_algebraicIndependent_of_isSeparable, followed by IntermediateField.topEquiv.

R -> K is formally smooth by Algebra.FormallySmooth.of_isLocalization. Composition therefore makes R -> L formally smooth. For the nonzero b from step 1, equip L with its canonical B-algebra via IsLocalization.Away.lift; verify both scalar towers by its defining equation. IsFractionRing.isFractionRing_of_isDomain_of_isLocalization shows L is the fraction field of B. Localization at the zero prime of B inverts all its nonzero elements, so IsLocalization.algEquiv identifies that local ring with L as an R-algebra. Transporting formal smoothness along this equivalence gives Algebra.IsSmoothAt R (0 : Ideal B).

Since B is finitely presented over R, Mathlib Algebra.IsSmoothAt.exists_notMem_smooth gives a nonzero c in B such that B[1/c] is smooth over R. Let d in S be its localization numerator using IsLocalization.Away.sec. IsLocalization.Away.associated_sec_fst shows image(d) and c are associated, so d is nonzero. By IsLocalization.Away.mul_of_associated, B[1/c] is the localization of S away from b*d. The canonical localization equivalence transfers smoothness to S[1/(b*d)]. The product is nonzero since S is a domain.
